# `tests/classify-corpus/` — hand-labeled classifier ground truth

**Nothing in this directory is generated by a test.** These files are the
frozen ground truth `crates/rf-classify/tests/eval.rs` grades against; the test
opens them read-only and checks every file's SHA-256 against
`MANIFEST.sha256` before *and* after scoring. If you change a label, you must
change `MANIFEST.sha256` in the same commit and say why in
`docs/classifier-eval.md`.

This replaces `tests/fixtures-labeled.jsonl`, which the old
`classification_gate` **wrote on every run** (`CLS-11`) and whose "ground
truth" therefore could never disagree with the code, and the labeler in
`eval.rs` that claimed to be independent but was the classifier's own rule
tables retyped (`CLS-01`).

Results, per-architecture precision/recall, and the list of what is *not*
measured: `docs/classifier-eval.md`.

---

## Record format (JSON Lines, one object per gadget)

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `fixture` | file under `tests/fixtures/` the gadget came from |
| `arch` | `Arch::slice_name()` — `x86_64`, `i386`, `arm`, `arm64`, `mips`, `ppc`, `sparc`, `riscv64` |
| `vaddr`, `bytes`, `text`, `delay_slot` | the scanner record, verbatim |
| `truth_primary` | **hand-assigned** primary class (R10). No code produced this field. |
| `truth_labels` | **hand-assigned** multi-label set (R9), sorted |
| `uncertain` | the ground truth itself is contested → excluded from **both** metrics |
| `labels_uncertain` | one *label* is contested but the primary class is not → excluded from the label-set metric only |
| `rules` | the rule ids applied (`R2`…`R10`, plus the finding or resolution ids below) |
| `why` | one-line justification for **this** gadget — the artifact TAXONOMY.md claimed and never had |
| `labeler`, `labeled` | who assigned the label and when |
| `stratum` | which sampling stratum drew it |
| `provenance` | sampler, depth, stride, offset, filter, and index within the filtered list |

`eval.rs::corpus_records_are_well_formed` enforces the internal consistency of
every record: a non-`other` primary must appear in its own label set, `other`
means no label (except a bare `dispatcher`), and `why` must actually say
something.

## Sampling rule (deterministic, documented, re-runnable)

Every stratum was drawn by `crates/rf-classify/tests/sample_corpus.rs`, an
`#[ignore]`d tool that writes nothing and prints JSONL to stdout. The gadget
list is `rf_scan::scan_binary` at `depth = 10` in its own returned order
(deduplicated and alphabetically sorted — deterministic across runs and
platforms). Each stratum keeps **every k-th** gadget of the filtered list
starting at index 0. For the uniform strata *k* is the smallest prime at or
above `total / target`, so the sample is spread over the whole list and no
gadget was chosen for being interesting.

| file | fixture | filter | k | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x64bash.jsonl` | elf-x64-bash-v4.1.5.1 | — | 757 | 60 |
| `linuxx64.jsonl` | elf-Linux-x64 | — | 1471 | 30 |
| `pex64.jsonl` | pe-x64-cmd-v6.1.7601 | — | 631 | 20 |
| `linuxx86.jsonl` | elf-Linux-x86 | — | 1423 | 30 |
| `pex86.jsonl` | pe-x86-cmd-v6.1.7600 | — | 691 | 20 |
| `arm64.jsonl` | elf-ARM64-bash | — | 593 | 30 |
| `arm.jsonl` | elf-ARMv7-ls | — | 131 | 25 |
| `mips.jsonl` | elf-Mips-Defcon-20-pwn100 | — | 5333 | 25 |
| `ppc.jsonl` | elf-PowerPC-bash | — | 3491 | 25 |
| `sparc.jsonl` | elf-SparcV8-bash | — | 293 | 25 |
| `riscv64.jsonl` | elf-Linux-RISCV_64 | — | 13 | 24 |
| `indirect-x64.jsonl` | elf-x64-bash-v4.1.5.1 | last insn is an indirect branch | 181 | 28 |
| `indirect-x86.jsonl` | elf-Linux-x86 | last insn is an indirect branch | 271 | 14 |
| `indirect-arm64.jsonl` | elf-ARM64-bash | last insn is an indirect branch | 254 | 14 |
| `syscall-x64.jsonl` | elf-x64-bash-v4.1.5.1 | text contains `syscall` | 1 | 5 |
| `syscall-x86.jsonl` | elf-Linux-x86 | text contains `int 0x80` | 4 | 10 |
| `stackptr-x64.jsonl` | elf-x64-bash-v4.1.5.1 | text contains `rsp` | 139 | 27 |
| `long-x64.jsonl` | elf-x64-bash-v4.1.5.1 | >= 6 instructions | 21 | 26 |

**438 records.** The last seven strata are *enriched*: their filters are purely
textual (mnemonic and substring tests on the scanner's own output), contain no
classification logic, and never call `rf_classify`, so they remain independent
of the thing being measured — but they are **not** a random sample of a binary,
so class frequencies here say nothing about how common a class is in the wild.
They exist because the rare-but-important classes (`syscall`, `dispatcher`) and
the rules most likely to be wrong (R5/R10 on stack-pointer traffic, R10's
last-side-effect choice on long gadgets) are invisible in a uniform sample.

## Labeling protocol

Each gadget was labeled by reading its disassembly and applying
**TAXONOMY.md R1–R13 as amended by `docs/AUDIT-FINDINGS.md` CLS-02, CLS-03,
CLS-12 and CLS-13** — a specification written before the implementation was
corrected, not the implementation itself. `rf_classify` was never run to
produce a label. Where the taxonomy is silent (mostly the cross-ISA mappings),
the resolution was written down *first*, applied uniformly, and recorded in
each affected record's `rules` field:

| id | resolution |
|---|---|
| `D-STACKW` | A **stack read** earns no `mem-read` (R1); a **stack write** earns `mem-write` (CLS-13: the controlled value going into memory is the payload). Applied to `push`, `mov [rsp+n], r`, `sw $r, n($sp)`, `stw r, n(r1)`, `c.sdsp`. |
| `D-SPWB` | An SP write that is the *writeback of a load/store addressing mode* (`ldp x29, x30, [sp], #0x10`, `strt r2, [sp], #-n`) is the architecture's pop/push mechanism, so R1 applies and it is **not** a pivot. An SP write by a *data-processing* instruction (`add sp, sp, #n`, `mov esp, …`, `addiu $sp, …`, `addi r1, r1, …`, `c.addi16sp`) **is** a pivot (R5). This mirrors x86 exactly: `pop rbx` is not a pivot, `add rsp, 8` is. |
| `D-FUSEDPOP` | ARM's `pop {…, pc}` is one instruction that both returns and loads registers. The `pc` write is mechanism and is skipped (R10); the other register loads are payload and earn `reg-write` — the same principle CLS-13 applies to `ret imm16`. |
| `D-DELAY` | On MIPS/SPARC the terminating control transfer is skipped wherever it sits in the text, and the delay-slot instruction after it is scored normally, because it really executes. |
| `D-ZEROREG` | A write to a hardwired-zero register (`$zero`, `xzr`/`wzr`, `%g0`, RISC-V `zero`) is architecturally discarded and earns no `reg-write`. The instruction can still earn `arithmetic` (R6 is mnemonic-only). |
| `D-ADR` | Address-formation instructions (`adrp`, `adr`, `auipc`) are the analogue of x86 `lea`, which R6 lists explicitly, so they earn `arithmetic` + `reg-write`. **This is a mapping choice, not a rule from the document** — see docs/classifier-eval.md, which counts the entries that depend on it. |
| `D-WINDOW` | SPARC `save`/`restore` change `%sp` through the register window. They are SPARC's `leave`, which R5 names explicitly, so they earn `stack-pivot`. |
| `D-SUBREG` | R8 asks whether an earlier arithmetic instruction "advances" the branch target register. Whether writing `al`/`eax` advances `rax`, or `w1` advances `x1`, is undecided by the rule. Entries whose *only* disagreement is this are marked `labels_uncertain` and excluded from the label-set metric. |
| `D-LOOP` | `loop`/`loopne` decrement `rcx`, but R7 labels only **non-control** instructions and a mid-gadget backward branch is control flow, so they earn no `reg-write`. |

### Verification, and its limits

The labeler is a language model that had **already read `crates/rf-classify/src/x86.rs`**
(the CLS-01 evidence in `docs/classifier-eval.md` required extracting its
mnemonic sets). It is therefore *not* a blind labeler, and the x86-64 result
below should be read with that in mind. What makes the corpus non-circular is
narrower and checkable: no label was produced by running `rf_classify`, every
label carries a written reason, and the files are frozen by hash.

As an independent check, all 270 x86/x64 records were cross-decoded with
**capstone** — a different decoder from the iced-x86 the classifier uses — and
the hand labels compared against its operand-access and register-access
metadata:

* memory labels: **18 of 270** disagreed. **Fourteen** are capstone metadata
  defects, each verified by hand against the Intel SDM: `lea` reported as a
  memory *read* (4), the multi-byte `nop dword ptr [rax]` reported as a read
  (2), `movlps m64, xmm` reported as a read rather than a write (1), the
  implicit string/port memory accesses of `insb`, `outsb`, `outsd` and `xlatb`
  not reported at all (5), and `ror m8, cl` / `rol m32, 1` reported without
  their write (2). **Three** are the checker itself treating every `push`
  operand as a stack operand, when the source `[rbp + rax + 0x49]` is an
  ordinary non-stack read. **One** — `cmpxchg dword ptr [rax], esi` at
  `linuxx64.jsonl:0x424583` — is a genuine dispute about whether the memory
  operand counts as written when the compare fails, and the primary class turns
  on it. That one is the corpus's single `uncertain: true` record and is
  excluded from every metric.
* register-write labels: **4 of 270** disagreed — two `loop`/`loopne` gadgets
  (resolved by `D-LOOP`: capstone reports the `rcx` decrement, R7 excludes
  control instructions) and two `aaa` gadgets, where capstone does not report
  the AL/AH write the SDM specifies.

The non-x86 records could not be cross-checked this way: capstone implements
`cs_regs_access` for AArch64, ARM, BPF, M680X, SH, TriCore and X86 only, so on
MIPS, PowerPC, SPARC and RISC-V there is no second metadata source to compare
against. Those labels rest on the ISA manuals and the printed operands alone.
